skill.name: find-skills
skill.description: Helps users find, compare, and install agent skills from the open skills ecosystem.
skill.summary: Finds relevant agent skills and guides users through evaluation and installation choices.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: The skill primarily contains legitimate marketplace discovery guidance, and several static hits are Markdown false positives. Real risk remains because the skill instructs agents to run npx-based Skills CLI commands, install third-party skills, and use global installation with skipped confirmation prompts.

remediation.issue: Global install command skips confirmation prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the skipped-confirmation option from examples and require an explicit user confirmation immediately before installation.

remediation.issue: The skill relies on npx for search, install, update, and init workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that npx may execute external package-manager code, and show the exact command before running it.

remediation.issue: Third-party skill installation is based mainly on popularity and source reputation checks.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to inspect the skill source, permissions, and recent changes before installation.

static_findings.snippet: The Skills CLI (`npx skills`) is the package manager for the open agent skills ecosystem. Skills are
- `npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword, optio
- `npx skills add <package>` - Install a skill from GitHub or other sources
- `npx skills check` - Check for skill updates
- `npx skills update` - Update all installed skills
- `vercel-labs/agent-skills` — React, Next.js, web design (100K+ installs each)
- User asks "how do I make my React app faster?" → `npx skills find react performance`
- User asks "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `npx skills find pr review`
- User asks "I need to create a changelog" → `npx skills find changelog`

content.value_statement: Users often do not know which agent skill can help with a task. This skill guides discovery, comparison, and installation choices using the Skills CLI and skills.sh.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when a user request may benefit from an installable skill.
Recommends checking the skills.sh leaderboard before deeper searches.
Shows how to search, add, check, update, and initialize skills with the Skills CLI.
Uses install count, source reputation, and repository stars as quality signals.
Structures recommendations with skill name, source, install count, install guidance, and a reference link.
Provides fallback guidance when no matching skill is found.
limitations: It depends on the availability and accuracy of skills.sh and the Skills CLI.
It does not perform a full security review of third-party skill source code.
Search quality depends on the user query and marketplace metadata.
Installation and update actions should require explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Find development helpers
use_cases.description: Locate skills for React, testing, deployment, documentation, or code review tasks.

use_cases.title: Compare marketplace options
use_cases.description: Review multiple skills using install counts, sources, and repository signals before choosing one.

use_cases.title: Extend an AI assistant
use_cases.description: Discover skills that add focused workflows to Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

prompt_templates.title: Find a basic skill
prompt_templates.scenario: A user knows the task but not the right skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a skill that can help me with React performance. Show one or two strong options and explain why they fit.

prompt_templates.title: Search a specific domain
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants focused marketplace results.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for skills related to end-to-end testing. Prefer maintained sources and include install counts when available.

prompt_templates.title: Compare before installing
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants a safer recommendation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare three skills for API documentation work. Include source reputation, repository signals, and any reasons to be cautious.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a safe installation
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants to add a selected skill after review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me review this skill before installation. Summarize what it does, what source it comes from, and what approval you need from me.

output_examples.input: Can you find a skill for improving a Next.js app?
output_examples.output: A suitable recommendation would include a web performance skill from a reputable source, its install count, why it matches the task, and a link for review.

output_examples.input: I need help creating changelogs repeatedly.
output_examples.output: The response should search for changelog or release-note skills, compare useful matches, and offer direct help if no strong skill exists.
The response should review source reputation, recent project signals, likely permissions, and ask for explicit approval before any installation.

best_practices: Clarify the user goal and domain before searching.
Check popularity, source reputation, and repository signals before recommending a skill.
Ask for explicit approval before installing, updating, or creating skills.
anti_patterns: Installing the first search result without reviewing its source.
Skipping confirmation prompts during global installation.
Using broad search terms when specific domain terms are available.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users find installable agent skills and evaluate whether those skills fit a task.

faq.question: Does it install skills automatically?
faq.answer: It can provide installation guidance, but installation should happen only after explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How does it judge skill quality?
faq.answer: It considers install count, source reputation, repository stars, and whether the skill matches the user task.

faq.question: Can it find skills outside web development?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers categories such as testing, DevOps, documentation, design, and productivity.

faq.question: What should users review before installing?
faq.answer: Users should review the source, purpose, recent changes, and any commands or permissions the skill may use.
